title: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models
authors: Shunyu Yao, Jeffrey Zhao, Dian Yu, Nan Du, Izhak Shafran, Karthik Narasimhan, Yuan Cao
lab: Princeton University (Yao, Narasimhan); Google Research, Brain team (the rest). Yao did the work as a Google intern
date: October 2022 (arXiv v1, 6 October 2022); v3, 10 March 2023, adds the GPT-3 appendix; published at ICLR 2023

code.title: ysymyth/ReAct
code.note: the authors' GPT-3 prompting code (MIT licence): one notebook per task, the Wikipedia environment (wikienv.py) and every prompt. PaLM, the model behind the main results, was never released, so the repository reruns the method on text-davinci-002, which OpenAI shut down on 4 January 2024 (its deprecations page), so the notebooks need a current model swapped in. The project page, react-lm.github.io, links it. About 20 minutes for the README and the HotpotQA notebook

takeaway: Interleaving free-form thoughts with environment actions in one prompted loop beats reasoning-only and acting-only baselines (HotpotQA/FEVER grounding, 71% ALFWorld, +10% WebShop) and is the template every modern agent loop descends from.
verdict: Believe the mechanism and the decision-making wins: the ALFWorld and WebShop gaps are three to six standard errors wide, from one or two exemplars. Treat the HotpotQA and FEVER orderings as inside the noise, and read ALFWorld's 71% as the best of six prompts picked on the test games (the average prompt scores 57%).

headline.d: two in-context games against BUTLER trained on 10<sup>5</sup> expert trajectories per task type (best trials; the average ReAct prompt scores 57%)

headline.k: WebShop, one-shot ReAct against imitation learning
headline.d: 500 test instructions; IL+RL 28.7%, Act 30.1%, human experts 59.6%

headline.k: caused by hallucination, ReAct against CoT
headline.d: HotpotQA, 200 hand-labelled trajectories; ReAct's own failures are mostly reasoning errors (47%), loops included
